question: In which of the following Articles is fundamental duties, like protecting public property and renouncing violence, stated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51A**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution specifies the **fundamental duties** of every citizen of India.
 
• These duties include protecting public property, renouncing violence, promoting harmony, and upholding the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• Fundamental duties were added to the Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act in 1976**.
 
• The inclusion of these duties aims to remind citizens that while enjoying their rights, they also have obligations towards the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 42nd Amendment Act** is often referred to as the "**Mini-Constitution**" due to its wide-ranging changes to the Constitution.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.
 
• **Fundamental duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union**.
 
• Originally, there were ten fundamental duties; however, the **86th Amendment Act added an eleventh duty**, which emphasizes the importance of providing opportunities for education to children.
 
• While fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are **not enforceable by law**, they serve as a moral guide for citizens.
